entries.summary: BLOCKER: booking fails to boot on commons 1.0.31 — split logback (core 1.5.38 vs classic 1.5.18) -> NoSuchMethodError LoggerContext.initCollisionMaps()
entries.detail:
booking/pom.xml bumped 1.0.27-SNAPSHOT -> 1.0.31-SNAPSHOT. `mvn -pl booking clean package` = BUILD SUCCESS (shaded jar contains commons/cloud-sdk-api/cloud-sdk-aws 1.0.31-SNAPSHOT). App boot FAILED immediately:

java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'void ch.qos.logback.classic.LoggerContext.initCollisionMaps()'
  at ch.qos.logback.classic.LoggerContext.reset(LoggerContext.java:381)
  at io.dropwizard.logging.common.DefaultLoggingFactory.configureLoggers(DefaultLoggingFactory.java:222)
  at io.dropwizard.core.cli.ConfiguredCommand.run(ConfiguredCommand.java:94)
  at com.inttra.mercury.booking.BookingApplication.main(BookingApplication.java:325)

Resolved classpath: ch.qos.logback:logback-core:1.5.38 + ch.qos.logback:logback-classic:1.5.18 (split logback).

Origin (dependency:tree -Dverbose):
- commons-1.0.31-SNAPSHOT.pom NEW: <exclusion> ch.qos.logback:logback-core from io.dropwizard:dropwizard-core:5.0.2, AND a direct <dependency> ch.qos.logback:logback-core:1.5.38 compile. commons-1.0.27-SNAPSHOT.pom has NO logback declarations at all.
- dynamo-integration-test-1.0.31-SNAPSHOT.pom declares ch.qos.logback:logback-classic:1.5.18 (unchanged behaviour; Maven nearest-wins picks 1.5.18 at depth 2 and widens its scope to compile even though dynamo-integration-test itself is test-scope in booking).
- dropwizard-core 5.0.2 would otherwise supply the matched pair logback-classic/core 1.5.33 (both "omitted for conflict").

Net: at 1.0.27 both classic and core resolved to 1.5.18 (consistent, app booted). At 1.0.31 core jumps to 1.5.38 while classic stays 1.5.18 -> ContextBase.initCollisionMaps() no longer present in the pairing -> hard boot failure for EVERY consumer of commons 1.0.31, not just booking.

ROOT CAUSE IS UPSTREAM in mercury-services-commons: pinning logback-core without pinning logback-classic to the same version. Recommended upstream fix: align dynamo-integration-test's logback-classic to 1.5.38 (or add a logback dependencyManagement pair in the commons parent).</detail>

entries.summary: FIX: pinned logback-classic + logback-core to 1.5.38 via booking dependencyManagement; boot restored
entries.detail:
booking/pom.xml (2 edits):
1. <mercury.commons.version> 1.0.27-SNAPSHOT -> 1.0.31-SNAPSHOT
2. New <logback.version>1.5.38</logback.version> property + logback-classic/logback-core entries in the existing <dependencyManagement> block (same block that already pins jackson-bom for the identical nearest-wins reason).

Rationale: commons 1.0.31 excludes logback-core from dropwizard-core and pins logback-core 1.5.38, while dynamo-integration-test 1.0.31 pins logback-classic 1.5.18. Maven nearest-wins then produced a split logback pair -> NoSuchMethodError at boot. dependencyManagement forces both halves to 1.5.38 (chosen over 1.5.18 to keep commons' security intent).

Verification after fix: mvn -pl booking dependency:tree shows logback-core 1.5.38 + logback-classic 1.5.38.

RESIDUAL (non-fatal, logged as WARN once at boot):
  LogbackAccessRequestLog - For logback-core, expected version 1.5.32 but found 1.5.38
  (dropwizard's logback-access-common/jetty12 2.0.12 is compiled against 1.5.32). Access logging works.

UPSTREAM FOLLOW-UP still recommended in mercury-services-commons: align logback-classic in dynamo-integration-test to 1.5.38, or add a logback dependencyManagement pair in the commons parent, so every consumer of commons 1.0.31 does not need this local workaround. Consumers still on older commons that upgrade to 1.0.31 (auth, booking-bridge, db-migration, registration, tx-tracking, network, rates, value-added-service, visibility, webbl, bill-of-lading-v2, watermill) will hit the same boot failure.</detail>

entries.summary: CONFIRMED via javap: bumping logback-classic to 1.5.38 in dynamo-integration-test alone fixes ALL consumers — no consumer-side pom change needed
entries.detail:
Bytecode proof (javap) that logback-classic 1.5.18 is the SOLE offender:

ContextBase (logback-core):
  1.5.18 -> protected void initCollisionMaps();  public void reset();
  1.5.33 -> (initCollisionMaps REMOVED)          public void reset();
  1.5.38 -> (initCollisionMaps REMOVED)          public void reset();

LoggerContext.reset() body (logback-classic):
  1.5.18 -> ... invokevirtual initCollisionMaps:()V ...   <-- NoSuchMethodError against core >= 1.5.33
  1.5.33 -> (no such call)

=> Bumping logback-classic in dynamo-integration-test from 1.5.18 to 1.5.38 IS sufficient; no consumer pom needs changing:
 - Consumers WITH dynamo-integration-test: classic 1.5.38 (depth 2) + core 1.5.38 -> exact match.
 - Consumers WITHOUT dynamo-integration-test: classic 1.5.33 from dropwizard-core 5.0.2 + core 1.5.38 -> compatible (1.5.33 no longer calls initCollisionMaps).

Still RECOMMENDED to additionally add a managed logback-classic + logback-core pair to the commons parent dependencyManagement so the pairing can never drift again (dependencyManagement beats transitive depth entirely).

Corroborating evidence from the OWASP scan: booking/suppressions.xml has a rule
  pkg:maven/ch.qos.logback/logback-core@1.5.18 -> CVE-2025-11226
which now reports ZERO MATCHES. That CVE is the reason commons pinned logback-core 1.5.38, confirming the fix direction must be UP to 1.5.38, not down to 1.5.18. The suppression rule is now stale and can be deleted.</detail>
<parameter name="references">["booking/pom.xml", "booking/suppressions.xml", "booking/docs/2026-08-16-booking-app-checkout-1.0.31-SNAPSHOT.md"]

entries.summary: Added reusable dependency-check.sh runner at repo root + booking checkout doc
entries.detail:
NEW FILE: dependency-check.sh (repo root, chmod +x). Module-agnostic OWASP dependency-check runner.

Usage: ./dependency-check.sh <module> [options]
  -j/--jar, -o/--out, -s/--suppression, -p/--project, -f/--format,
  --fail-on-cvss, -n/--no-update, --purge, --no-summary, -h/--help

Key behaviours:
- Auto-detects shaded jar(s) in <module>/target, excluding original-*, *-sources, *-javadoc, *-tests.
- Suppression resolution: <module>/suppressions.xml then repo-root suppressions.xml.
- CREATES the output dir (default <module>/target/owasp). The user's original command failed with
  "Invalid 'out' argument: 'owasp' - path does not exist" because dependency-check will NOT mkdir.
- Nested modules supported (network/server, visibility/visibility-inbound).
- SECURITY: NVD_API_KEY written to a chmod 600 mktemp property file as nvd.api.key and passed via
  --propertyfile instead of --nvdApiKey, so the key is not visible in the process list. trap removes it on exit.
- Windows/Git Bash: cygpath -w conversion + MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL="*" so args are not mangled for
  dependency-check.bat. Resolves dependency-check | .bat | .sh from PATH.
- Prints a severity roll-up + all CRITICAL/HIGH findings from the JSON report after the run.

Bug found and fixed during testing: the summary passed an MSYS path (/c/Users/...) to a native Windows
python -> FileNotFoundError. Fixed by wrapping the report path in to_native().

Also created booking/docs/2026-08-16-booking-app-checkout-1.0.31-SNAPSHOT.md documenting the whole checkout.
NOTE: .gitignore:110 has `**/docs/`, so ALL module docs folders are untracked, including that file. Flagged
in the doc (section 9) with a suggested `!**/docs/*.md` negation; not changed since it is repo-wide.

Temp helper scripts booking/target/check-prereqs.ps1 and run-depcheck.ps1 were removed after use.</detail>

entries.summary: CLARIFIED: no DynamoDB tables were created — "Creating ... repository" = in-JVM object binding; INT tables date from 2018-2019 and were untouched
entries.detail:
Question raised: the checkout doc said "DynamoDB repositories created" — did the app create tables in INT? NO. Wording was misleading; doc section 6.3-6.5 corrected.

The boot line "Creating <Entity> composite-key repository for table: inttra_int_booking_X" is emitted by booking's OWN BookingDynamoModule, BEFORE the SDK call, and refers to constructing an in-JVM DatabaseRepository object (Guice singleton wrapping a DynamoDbEnhancedClient table handle). It is not a CreateTable API call.

EVIDENCE 1 — the factory cannot create tables (bytecode scan of cloud-sdk-aws-1.0.31-SNAPSHOT.jar):
  javap -c -p DynamoRepositoryFactory | grep -ic 'createTable|describeTable'  ->  0
  grep -rl "createTable" --include=*.class .  ->  only
      com.inttra.mercury.cloudsdk.database.command.DynamoDbAdminCommand
      com.inttra.mercury.cloudsdk.database.util.DynamoDbAdminUtil
  Table creation lives solely in DynamoDbAdminCommand.createTableWithGsisIfNotExists(...), reachable ONLY via the
  opt-in `dynamo-create` CLI command. We ran `server`. BookingDynamoDbAdminCommand is merely REGISTERED in the
  bootstrap (hence "initialized with 7 entity classes" on every start, even --help); registration != execution.

EVIDENCE 2 — createEnhancedRepository call graph is entirely in-process:
  validateConfig(clientConfig)
  createDynamoDbClient(clientConfig)                      // lazy client, no connection
  DynamoDbEnhancedClient.builder().dynamoDbClient(..).build()
  new EnhancedDynamoRepository(client, enhancedClient, tableName, domainType, config)
  The table name is just a String handed to the enhanced client; nothing hits AWS until a real read/write.

EVIDENCE 3 — aws dynamodb describe-table shows the INT tables long predate this work and kept their data:
  inttra_int_booking_BookingDetail              2018-06-07  588 items
  inttra_int_booking_UniqueId                   2018-06-07    1
  inttra_int_booking_SequenceId                 2019-02-21    1
  inttra_int_booking_RapidReservation           2018-08-24   10
  inttra_int_booking_SpotRatesDetail            2019-10-04    0
  inttra_int_booking_SpotRatesToInttraRefDetail 2019-10-15   11
  inttra_int_booking_Template                   2018-10-03   18
  (Template + TemplateSummary are two repositories over ONE physical table.)

EVIDENCE 4 — bogus-credential boot died at the FIRST genuine AWS call, which is SSM, before the Dynamo module ran:
  software.amazon.awssdk.services.ssm.model.SsmException: The security token included in the request is invalid.
  Confirms SSM is the first live call and that Dynamo wiring is offline.</detail>

entries.summary: Fixed dependency-check.sh output location (mvn clean was deleting reports) + added full explanatory comments; re-ran booking and tx-tracking
entries.detail:
ISSUE FOUND: booking/target/owasp had vanished. Root cause: `mvn -pl booking clean package` (run twice afterwards for the logback fix verification) deletes the entire target/ directory, taking the OWASP reports with it. Reports must not live under target/.

FIX in dependency-check.sh:
- Default output dir changed from <module>/target/owasp to <repo-root>/owasp-reports/<module>.
  Survives `mvn clean`, keeps every module's reports side by side, one place to gitignore.
- Added `owasp-reports/` to .gitignore (line 113) so generated reports don't pollute git status.
- Removed the stale tx-tracking/target/owasp directory.

DOCUMENTATION: rewrote dependency-check.sh with thorough explanatory comments -
- File header: purpose, quick start, common uses, why we scan the SHADED JAR not the pom
  (fat jars: scanning the jar reports what actually ships, including shaded transitives),
  and requirements.
- Explained `set -euo pipefail` flag by flag.
- Explained REPO_ROOT derivation from BASH_SOURCE (run from any cwd).
- Explained MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL (stops Git Bash mangling args for the .bat launcher).
- Explained the `[[ -t 1 ]]` colour guard (plain text when piped/CI).
- Explained to_native()/cygpath and why BOTH the .bat launcher and native Windows python need it.
- Explained resolve_cli() trying dependency-check | .bat | .sh.
- Explained why SCAN_TARGETS/SUPPRESSIONS are arrays (repeatable flags).
- Explained ${1%/} trailing-slash strip from tab completion.
- Explained each jar exclusion: original-* (pre-shade, double counts), -sources, -javadoc, -tests.
- Explained the `while IFS= read -r` loop (filenames with spaces).
- Explained mkdir -p: dependency-check does NOT create --out and fails with

entries.summary: CORRECTION: no HIGH findings exist — booking 55 MEDIUM, tx-tracking 14 MEDIUM. My summary wrongly used cvssv3.baseSeverity instead of dependency-check's own severity field
entries.detail:
User challenged: "I did not see any HIGHs" in the HTML report. User was RIGHT; my summary script was wrong.

ROOT CAUSE: my summary read `cvssv3.baseSeverity` from the JSON. dependency-check publishes its OWN
reconciled verdict in the top-level `severity` field, and that is what the HTML renders. The tool prefers the
newer CVSS v4 score when the CNA published one.

Example CVE-2026-34478 (log4j-core 2.23.1):
  "severity": "MEDIUM"                      <- tool verdict, shown in HTML
  cvssv3.baseScore 7.5, baseSeverity HIGH   <- what my script wrongly used
  cvssv4 vector AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:L/SA:N  (source security@apache.org)
  -> v4 shows no confidentiality/integrity/availability impact on the vulnerable system, hence MEDIUM.

CORRECTED COUNTS (dependency-check severity == HTML):
  booking     : 55 findings / 9 vulnerable deps -> MEDIUM 55.  ZERO Critical/High.
  tx-tracking : 14 findings / 6 vulnerable deps -> MEDIUM 14.  ZERO Critical/High.
Previously reported "booking 6 HIGH / tx-tracking 4 HIGH" was an artifact of the wrong field. Retract those.

Mismatched CVEs (CVSS v3 HIGH but tool MEDIUM): CVE-2026-34478/34479/34480 (7.5, log4j) and
CVE-2026-65898 (7.2, swagger-ui, booking only).

FIX in dependency-check.sh summary block:
- Primary severity now `vuln['severity']` (tool verdict) so the console summary always matches the HTML.
- Score shown is cvssv3.baseScore or cvssv4.baseScore.
- Prints "No CRITICAL or HIGH findings." when clean.
- New de-duplicated FYI section listing CVEs whose CVSS v3 rating is HARSHER than the tool verdict, so the
  stricter v3 view is not lost but does not inflate the headline counts.
Both modules re-scanned with the corrected logic; output now agrees with the HTML reports.

Corrected booking/docs/2026-08-16-booking-app-checkout-1.0.31-SNAPSHOT.md sections 7.1, 7.2 and follow-up 6.

LESSON: for OWASP dependency-check JSON, the authoritative severity is the top-level `severity` field.
Do NOT derive severity from cvssv3.baseSeverity — it disagrees with the report the humans read.</detail>
